prompt: Hallam & Vasey, steel detailers, are issuing sheet S-A103 for the Immingham blending plant mezzanine, an elevation of each frame on one A1: the drum-store frame left, the packing-line frame right. The drum-store frame is four storeys high and twelve metres between end columns on a four-metre grid; the packing-line frame is two storeys, twenty-four metres between end columns on the same grid. Columns 152 UC, beams 254 UB, bracing equal angle. The erector's instruction, quoted on the sheet, is that every column line and every beam line must end up drawn into a single braced system, and that, with that met, he wants as few diagonals as the frames allow, each cut and priced singly. Office convention marks a braced panel with a heavy solid diagonal, the rest left blank. Wanted is the checking photograph of the finished sheet: the A1 flat on the plan table under the drawing-office lights, shot square from straight above, whole sheet in frame with both elevations and the title block, nothing cropped.
easy_question: Does this picture show a structural steel drawing sheet with two braced frame elevations drawn side by side and a title block in the corner? Answer yes or no.

steps.ask: How many panels on the left-hand frame elevation carry a diagonal bar?
How many panels on the right-hand frame elevation are left blank?
